analysis:
The only change in ProviderLoop.swift adds `operatorModelFilter: Set<String>?` (head lines 221-224) and initializes it in init (head ~946-948). It is `enabled_models` from config, unioned with the start-selection model IDs, and nil when `enabled_models` is empty. In this PR it is stored state only. The shown diff has no readers, no enforcement and no behavior change. A comment mentions `operatorFilterAllows`, which is not in the supplied evidence.

Security relevance: the filter looks like an operator-side allowlist restricting which coordinator-pushed models the provider will load or serve. That touches TB-002 (coordinator-to-provider contract) and TB-007 (inference engine). It also touches A-004 (model weights) and A-018 (serving availability).

I found no regression. Nothing is weakened: no existing check is removed, and the filter is not consumed here. The base init still builds `advertisedModels` and `ordinaryServingModelIDs` unchanged.

Open integration questions for the next pass, all outside the supplied evidence:
- Where `operatorFilterAllows` is implemented and whether it is enforced on every path that loads or advertises a model. Those paths include `desired_models`, `prefetch_model`, preload, the autopilot inventory and the autopilot download coordinator.
- Whether the nil case, which means any coordinator-pushed model is allowed, matches existing behavior.
- Whether the filter is updated consistently on live model switches (`modelSwitchTask`) and the persisted switch state.
- Whether the T-041 prefix-cache affected files are untouched. In this unit they are.

The threat model may need a note on the filter if it becomes an enforced control.
